proposal.utterance: Classify 'an act of promising' in BFO terms.

entities.label: ActOfPromising
entities.rationale: An act of promising is a temporally extended happening — an occurrent process — in which an agent performs a speech act creating a commitment. It unfolds in time, has temporal parts, and involves participants. It is therefore a subclass of BFO Process (BFO_0000015). It is a common noun denoting a kind, so it is a class, not an individual.

relations.rationale: ActOfPromising is a kind of Process: it unfolds in time, involves at least one agent participant, and terminates in the creation of a normative commitment. Subclassing BFO_0000015 (Process) correctly situates it in the occurrent branch.

open_questions: Should ActOfPromising be further typed to distinguish it as a speech act process? If so, we might introduce an intermediate class such as 'SpeechActProcess' (also a BFO_0000015 subclass) as its parent.

Is the resulting commitment (the promise as an information artifact or normative content) also of interest? If so, we could additionally model a 'PromissoryObligation' as a Role (BFO_0000023) borne by the promisor, and/or a 'PromissoryContent' as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031) instantiated by the act.

Are we interested in the individual token act (a specific act of promising by a specific person at a specific time, which would be an individual of type BFO_0000015) or only in the general kind? The utterance says 'an act of promising', suggesting the kind, but please confirm.
proposal.rationale_summary: An act of promising is paradigmatically an occurrent: it happens, unfolds through time, and has a beginning, middle, and end. In BFO 2020, occurrents that are happenings or doings of agents are classified as Processes (BFO_0000015). The act of promising involves at least one participant (the promisor, and typically an addressee) and produces a normative consequence (an obligation or commitment), but the act itself — the doing — is the process. Because the utterance uses the indefinite article ('an act of promising'), it invokes the kind rather than a specific token event, so ActOfPromising is introduced as a class (common noun) that is a rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000015. No existing working-ontology class already covers this kind, so a new class is minted. Secondary modelling choices — such as the resulting promissory obligation as a Role inhering in the promisor, or the propositional content of the promise as a Generically Dependent Continuant — are flagged as open questions awaiting user direction.
